correctness.rationale: In the literal recursion, position t uses a_{1+ν₂(t)}. Counting each valuation in a prefix gives its Gray parity t XOR (t shifted right by one); the Gray map is injective, and flipping its highest bit complements the binary index. This rules out a nonwrapping tangram and gives the unique wrapping start N−d for every positive admissible half-length d. Independently, every nonempty linear factor contains its highest-ranked letter exactly once: it contains the central letter or lies in one smaller copy. Thus no two distinct prefixes have equal parity. The word is a palindrome, so in any wrap the suffix and prefix have cancelling parity exactly when their lengths match; those two equal-length blocks are reversals. An abelian cube would give two length-2d abelian squares at distinct starts, impossible since 3d≤N. Rank 1 has no admissible positive d. checker.py was inspected, not executed; the rank-1–8 checks described there cover parity and the square/tangram sets, not a separate cube enumeration.
